text.p: Jose Maria Olazabal hopes to emerge from 18 months of pain and depression when he reappears on the professional tour at the Dubai Desert Classic starting next Thursday.

The 1994 U.S. Masters champion, who has not played since September 1995 because of problems with his right foot, has decided to accept an invitation to play following "big improvements" to his health in recent weeks.
"I now consider most of my physical problems to be behind me," said the Spaniard, who was originally diagnosed as having rheumatoid arthritis after withdrawing from the 1995 Ryder Cup team.
Now 31, Olazabal is refusing to commit himself to any further tournaments for the moment.

"The Desert Classic will be a full test in real competition conditions and I will take stock of the situation following the tournament. I do no intend to make a schedule now...I will take it week by week."
Olazabal has played in four Ryder Cups and collected 22 tournament titles worldwide in his career prior to his foot problems.
PGA European Tour executive director Ken Schofield said: "We share with Jose Maria his delight at being able to return to Tour competition and look forward to him resuming his outstanding career."
